caption: Two jars of honey are tipped side by side, one straight from the fridge and one that sat in the sun; the warm honey pours out in a quick stream while the cold honey barely moves.

sa.check: Two jars of honey are tipped side by side.
One jar has been in the sun and one in the fridge.
The warm honey pours out in a stream.
The cold honey creeps or stays put.
Both jars are tipped at about the same moment.
The difference between the two is plain.

pc.expect: Both are thick liquids, the warm one running in a thinner faster stream and the cold one creeping as a stiff mass that holds its shape.
pc.fail: The cold honey pours out as freely as the warm one; or the warm honey stands as a rigid column as it leaves the jar; or the cold honey shatters as a solid; or the warm honey runs as thin as water and splashes.

pc.expect: Each honey only advances down and out and neither runs back up into its jar; the difference does not reverse.
pc.fail: The cold jar empties faster than the warm one; or a stream runs back up into its jar; or the warm honey stops and the cold one speeds up with nothing changed; or the honey climbs the jar's inner wall and stays.

pc.expect: Both honeys move downward out of the tipped jars and fall or pile below.
pc.fail: A honey runs upward out of a tipped jar; or a stream hangs in the air without falling; or the honey climbs the jar's outside; or a pile below rises back into a jar.

pc.expect: The jars show their contents moving: the warm jar's level drops while the cold jar's stays nearly still.
pc.fail: The warm jar's level stays unchanged while a stream pours from it; or the cold jar's level drops as fast as the warm one's; or honey pours from a jar that is plainly still upright and untipped.

pc.expect: Two jars of honey; the honey goes only from jar to the surface below and none appears from nowhere.
pc.fail: Honey appears below a jar with none leaving it; or a jar refills itself; or a third jar appears; or honey passes through a jar's wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The jars' labels, the honey's colour and the surface below stay the same.
pc.fail: A label changes; or the honey changes colour; or the surface below changes pattern.
